label: Size adjective (event 4061)
summary: Gives a size word picked by a number: sizeable, large, huge, mammoth, colossal or titanic.
details: It reads the character's variable 4061_size_adjective: 12 or more gives titanic, 10 or more colossal, 8 or more mammoth, 6 or more huge, 4 or more large, and anything lower sizeable (the fallback). Judging by the entry names it belongs to one event of the Roads to Power flavour set (ep3_laamp_flavour_ewan.4061). Titanic is shown in a stronger text style than the others. Runs on a character.

label: AI personality text
summary: Gives the name of the character's AI personality, with a small icon in front.
details: The game checks in this order: warlike, cautious, pious builder, economical boom, then conqueror (a variable named conqueror on the character). If none fits, the fallback economical unpredictable is shown. Each text is an icon plus a game-concept link to that personality. Runs on a character.

label: Abortifacient herb
summary: Gives the name of a herb used as an abortifacient, such as pennyroyal, catmint, thymbra, saffron or ergot.
details: There are 16 herbs. Each has a condition on where the character is (its location's region): for example pennyroyal fits Europe, Asia Minor, the Middle East and North Africa and counts three times as much as the others, while catmint fits everywhere. Because random picking is on, the game picks at random among the herbs whose condition holds. Runs on a character.

label: Accolade rank name
summary: Gives the rank name of an accolade (knight order), with its number in small text.
details: Seven entries: established (rank 1), recognized (2), feted (3), lionized (4), then august, glorious and unsung. The first four texts are shown in the input; the other three are not. Runs on a character.

label: Forehead or nose
summary: Gives either the word "forehead" or the word "nose".
details: Random picking is allowed, so the game may choose either one. Runs on a character.

label: Animal prestige rating
summary: Gives a one-line rating of how much prestige a hunted animal brings, on a scale of five.
details: The game reads the animal type saved on the activity: hare and fox give Trivial; wolf, hyena and lynx give Middling; boar, hart, elk, bison and aurochs give Impressive; bear, lion, tiger, leopard and exotic birds give the top rating. Any other animal gets the fallback, Mediocre (2/5). Runs on an activity (used in the hunt activity's files).

label: Animal danger rating
summary: Gives a one-line rating of how dangerous a hunted animal is, on a scale of five.
details: The text shows a death icon and the danger label, then a word and a score. The game reads the animal type saved on the activity: hare gives Harmless (1/5); fox, roe and gazelle give Mild (2/5); aurochs, boar, bison, hart and elk give Dangerous (4/5); bear, lion, tiger and leopard give the top level, Treacherous (5/5). Any other animal gets the fallback, Middling (3/5). Runs on an activity.

label: Exam score word
summary: Gives a word describing an exam result: heavenly, glorious, respectable or curious.
details: The game checks variables on the activity, in this order: has_perfect_score gives heavenly, has_great_score glorious, has_decent_score respectable, has_questionable_score curious. If none is set, nothing is shown. Runs on an activity (imperial examination).

label: Both or all (failed)
summary: Gives "Both" or "All", depending on how many family entrants failed the exam.
details: It reads the character's variable num_exam_family_entrants_failed: exactly 2 gives "Both", more than 2 gives "All". With fewer than 2 no entry fits and nothing is shown. The entries are named FaileesBoth and FaileesAll. Runs on a character.

label: Both or all (passed)
summary: Gives "Both" or "All", depending on how many family entrants passed the exam.
details: It reads the character's variable num_exam_family_entrants_passed: exactly 2 gives "Both", more than 2 gives "All". With fewer than 2 nothing is shown. It reuses the same texts as the "failed" version (FaileesBoth and FaileesAll). Runs on a character.

label: Admired feature
summary: Gives the name of a body feature someone might admire, such as bright eyes, a warm smile or strong hands.
details: There are 12 features (including bulging muscles, broad shoulders, towering height and nimble fingers). Random picking is allowed, so the game may choose any valid one. Runs on a character.

label: Fitting greeting
summary: Gives a greeting that fits how the character stands to another character (saved as scope:second): lover, liege, vassal, family or friend, foreign ruler, or a general fallback.
details: Checked in this order: the other is the character's lover; the character is a vassal of the other (the liege greeting); the other is a vassal of the character; the two are close or extended family, or friends; the other is a ruler at the top of a different realm; otherwise the fallback. Each text calls another custom text (such as GreetingToLover) on the root character, with the other character as second. Runs on a character.

label: Fitting unfriendly greeting
summary: Gives an unfriendly greeting that fits how the character stands to another character (saved as scope:second): liege, vassal, family, foreign ruler, or a fallback.
details: Same checks as AppropriateGreeting, but there is no lover entry and friends do not count as family (only close or extended family). Each text calls another custom text (such as GreetingToLiegeNegative) on the root character. Runs on a character.

label: Fitting friendly greeting
summary: Gives a friendly greeting that fits how the character stands to another character (saved as scope:second): lover, liege, vassal, family, foreign ruler, or a fallback.
details: Same checks as AppropriateGreeting, except friends do not count as family (only close or extended family). The lover entry is the plain lover greeting (greeting_appropriate_lover), shared with the neutral version; the others are the positive ones. Runs on a character.

label: Extra greeting line
summary: Gives a short extra line to follow a greeting, either a negative or a positive one, depending on how the character feels about the other.
details: Negative when the other is not the character's liege or above and the character's opinion of the other is -10 or lower; positive when the other is the character's liege or above, or the opinion is above -10. The other character is saved as scope:second. The key is spelled "Supplimentary" in the game. Each entry calls another custom text on the root character. Runs on a character.

label: Arm or arms
summary: Gives "arm" or "arms".
details: Used where the text must match one or two arms. Runs on a character.

label: Book content adverb
summary: Gives an adverb for how good a book's content is, such as excellently, deeply, insightfully, adequately or modestly.
details: One of five grades. Runs on a character.

label: Craft quality adverb
summary: Gives an adverb for how well an artifact was made: masterfully, excellently or finely.
details: Runs on a character.

label: Richness adverb
summary: Gives an adverb for how richly an artifact is decorated, such as extravagantly, opulently, lavishly or plainly.
details: There are 11 words. Random picking is allowed, so the game may choose any valid one. Runs on a character.

label: Animal adjective
summary: Gives an adjective for an animal, such as great, mighty, man-eating, black, white or cursed.
details: There are 17 words. Random picking is on, so the game picks any of them at random. Runs on an artifact.

label: Animal trinket part
summary: Gives the animal part a trinket is made from: antler, horn, tusk, claws, fangs, tail or foot.
details: Runs on an artifact.

label: Animal type
summary: Gives the name of an animal, from cat and dog to bear, lion, unicorn and dragon.
details: There are 26 animals, from cat and dog to bear, lion, unicorn and dragon. Runs on an artifact.

label: Armor artifact name
summary: Builds the name of an armor artifact: a prefix and quality word, the owner's culture or dynasty, or a descriptor, followed by the armor type.
details: Four forms: basic (name prefix, armor property and type), culture (owner's culture and type), dynasty (owner's dynasty and type), descriptor (armor property and type). It reads the newly made artifact and the root character. Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character.

label: Armor description
summary: Gives the description sentence of an armor artifact, chosen by its armor type: mail, plate, scale, lamellar, laminar, brigandine or a fallback.
details: The armor type is a saved flag (scope:armor_type, such as armor_type_mail); the first matching type is used, otherwise the fallback text. Each sentence fills in the artifact's material, quality words and cloth or cordage features. Runs on a character.

label: Armor type, lowercase
summary: Gives the armor type in lowercase, such as mail, plate armor, scale armor or lamellar armor.
details: Seven types, ending with shield. Runs on a character. The capitalised twin is ArtifactArmorTypeUppercase.

label: Armor type, capitalised
summary: Gives the armor type with capital letters, such as Mail, Plate Armor, Scale Armor or Lamellar Armor.
details: Seven types, ending with shield. Runs on a character. Used in artifact names. The lowercase twin is ArtifactArmorTypeLowercase.

label: Article and book quality
summary: Gives "an excellent", "a deep", "an insightful", "an adequate" or "a modest", with the right a or an.
details: Runs on a character. The same grades without the article are in ArtifactBookContentQuality.

label: Article and richness
summary: Gives "An extravagant", "An opulent", "A beautiful", "An elegant" and so on, with the right a or an and a capital letter.
details: Seven words, ending with plain. Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character.

label: Axe haft description
summary: Describes an axe's haft: an elegant haft with a decoration, or a sturdy plain one.
details: Both texts name the artifact's wood feature; the decorated one also uses its decoration feature. Runs on an artifact.

label: Axe head description
summary: Describes an axe's metal head, decorated or not, and says it is mounted on the haft that follows.
details: Both texts use the artifact's head metal feature; the decorated one also uses its head decoration. Other weapon heads reuse these texts. Runs on an artifact.

label: Weapon base type (artifact)
summary: Gives the weapon type as a plain noun: axe, hammer, mace, spear, dagger or sword.
details: It has the same entries as ArtifactWeaponBaseType, but runs on an artifact instead of a character. The entry order differs (dagger before sword here).

label: Book content quality
summary: Gives a word for how good a book's content is: excellent, deep, insightful, adequate or modest.
details: Runs on a character. Adverb and article forms exist as separate custom texts.

label: Book description
summary: Gives the description of a book artifact: one built on its title, one of five other wordings, or one for a book without a preface.
details: The texts fill in the book's topic and subject, and, through the owner's custom texts, the content quality, the quality of the lettering and how richly it is illuminated. Runs on an artifact.

label: Book subject
summary: Gives the topic a book is about, such as warfare, diplomacy, scholarly matters or stewardship.
details: There are 28 subjects, including skills, lifestyles, dynasty, empire, alchemy and religious text. Runs on a character.

label: Bow type
summary: Gives the bow kind with its article: a longbow, a composite bow, a crossbow or a bow.
details: Names suggest it is used for inspirations. Runs on a character.

label: Dagger decoration
summary: Describes how a dagger is decorated (hilt and blade, blade, hilt or none), using the sword texts.
details: Each entry only points to the matching sword decoration text, so daggers read like swords. Runs on an artifact.

label: Armor decoration
summary: Describes how a piece of armor is decorated, such as inlays, painted or etched patterns, thin lines, gold plating, lining, embossing or grouped rivets.
details: Eight variants. Several mention a repeating pattern taken from the artifact's decoration pattern feature. Runs on an artifact.

label: Elixir description
summary: Describes an elixir: one that restores lost youth or one that keeps death away forever.
details: The immortality text uses the name of the owner's faith's death deity. Random picking is allowed. Runs on an artifact.

label: Flower species
summary: Gives the name of a flower, such as aster, orchid, rose, poppy or tulip.
details: There are 23 entries, but lotus is listed twice. Runs on a character.

label: Flower species gender
summary: Picks a grammatical gender form for the flower species saved as scope:flower_species: one ending (_z) for orchid, rose, foxglove, geranium, lily, lavender, peony, delphinium, chrysanthemum and gardenia, the other (_m) for every other flower.
details: The game gives no text for either entry, only their keys (ArtifactFlowerSpecies_z and ArtifactFlowerSpecies_m). It lives in the game's Polish custom text file (00_pl_custom_loc.txt), so the endings probably stand for feminine and masculine forms; that is an inference from the file name. Runs on a character.

label: Hammer head description
summary: Describes a hammer's head, decorated or not, using the axe head texts.
details: Both entries only point to the axe head wording. Runs on an artifact.

label: Hammer shaft description
summary: Describes a hammer's shaft: an elegant decorated wooden shaft, or a sturdy plain one.
details: Both texts use the artifact's wood feature; the decorated one also uses its decoration feature. Runs on an artifact.

label: Mace handle description
summary: Describes a mace's handle: an elegant decorated metal handle, or a solid plain one.
details: Both texts use the artifact's handle metal feature; the decorated one also uses its metal handle decoration. Runs on an artifact.

label: Mace head description
summary: Describes a mace's head, decorated or not, using the axe head texts.
details: Both entries only point to the axe head wording. Runs on an artifact.

label: Marco Polo quote body
summary: Gives the main part of a Marco Polo quote shown in an artifact's description, with "(...)" added at the end.
details: Seven quotes, each taken from a matching quote text of the game. Random picking is allowed. Runs on an artifact. The intro and end parts are separate custom texts.

label: Marco Polo quote end
summary: Gives the closing part of a Marco Polo quote shown in an artifact's description.
details: Two quotes. Random picking is allowed. Runs on an artifact.

label: Marco Polo quote intro
summary: Gives the opening part of a Marco Polo quote shown in an artifact's description, with "(...)" added at the end.
details: Two quotes. Random picking is allowed. Runs on an artifact.

label: Artifact name prefix
summary: Gives the first word of an artifact's name: the owner's titled name, the owner's culture, the culture of where it was found, the owner's dynasty, the inspiration owner's name, or a quality word.
details: Nine entries: owner name, owner culture, location culture, owner dynasty, inspiration owner name, and four quality descriptors (high from a saved quality of 70 or more, two medium wordings, low). The owner and quality are saved scopes (scope:owner, scope:quality) that must exist. Location culture is used when the artifact's adventure location lies outside the owner's realm, and it names the culture of that province's holder. Random picking is on: the game picks at random among the entries that fit. Runs on a character. For artifacts that already exist, see ArtifactPrefixGenericAfterCreation.

label: Artifact name prefix (existing)
summary: Gives the first word of an artifact's name once the artifact exists: its owner's titled name, culture or dynasty, or a quality word such as "magnificent".
details: Seven entries: owner name, owner culture, owner dynasty (only if the owner has one) and four quality descriptors (high from a quality of 70 or more, two medium wordings from 40 to 69). It reads the owner from the artifact itself, unlike the plain prefix version, and the quality from the character's variable quality. Random picking is on. Runs on a character.

label: Artifact quality word
summary: Gives a word for how well an artifact is made: masterful, excellent, very fine or fine.
details: Runs on a character.

label: Small hide origin
summary: Says how a small animal hide was obtained: preserved to honour a pet, or hunted by a named hunter in a named barony.
details: The pet text uses the owner's "her/his". The hunt text reads the hunter and location saved on the artifact (adventure_artifact_hunter and adventure_artifact_location). Runs on an artifact.

label: Spear head description
summary: Describes a spear's head: a decorated one, a decorated one with a sentence about fins, or a plain one.
details: The decorated and plain ones reuse the axe head texts; the flanked one has its own sentence about a double-edged blade with thin fins. Both decorated entries have the same condition (the artifact has a head decoration) and the first match wins, so the fins entry comes second and is not reached through this key alone. The plain one is the last entry. Runs on an artifact.

label: Spear shaft description
summary: Describes a spear's shaft: decorated, plain, or plain with an extra sentence about elegance and deadliness.
details: All use the artifact's wood feature; the decorated one adds its decoration feature. Runs on an artifact.

label: Sword decoration
summary: Describes how a sword is decorated: hilt and blade, blade only, hilt only, or none.
details: Five entries: both hilt and blade decorated; only the blade; only the hilt; and two plain texts, the alternate one speaking of a strict, utilitarian look. The decorated texts use the artifact's hilt and blade decoration features. Runs on an artifact.

label: Artifact type word
summary: Gives a plain word for the kind of artifact, such as crown, weapon, armor, regalia, throne or book.
details: There are 32 kinds, from helmet to chest; each is picked by the artifact's type. Note that the helmet type reads as "crown". Runs on an artifact.

label: Flower species (artifact)
summary: Gives the name of a flower, such as aster, orchid, rose, poppy or tulip.
details: Same entries as ArtifactFlowerSpecies (lotus is listed twice here too) but it runs on an artifact instead of a character.

label: Richness word
summary: Gives a word for how richly an artifact is decorated: extravagant, opulent, beautiful, elegant, ornate, fancy or plain.
details: Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character.

label: Weapon base type
summary: Gives the weapon type as a plain noun: axe, hammer, mace, spear, sword or dagger.
details: Runs on a character. The same list for artifacts is ArtifactBaseWeaponType.

label: Weapon type with article
summary: Gives the weapon type with its article: an axe, a hammer, a mace, a spear, a sword or a dagger.
details: Runs on a character.

label: Girls or boys
summary: Gives "girls" or "boys", whichever the character is attracted to.
details: Attracted to women only gives girls; to men only gives boys. If attracted to both: the same sex as the character when the rite check homosexuality_accepted holds, the opposite sex when not. If attracted to neither: the opposite sex. Runs on a character.

label: Woman or man
summary: Gives "woman" or "man", whichever the character is attracted to.
details: Attracted to women only gives woman; to men only gives man. If attracted to both: the same sex as the character when the rite check homosexuality_accepted holds, the opposite sex when not. If attracted to neither: the opposite sex. Runs on a character.

label: A woman or a man
summary: Gives "a woman" or "a man", whichever the character is attracted to.
details: Same rules as AttractionWomanMan: one sex if attracted to only that sex; if attracted to both, the same sex as the character when the rite check homosexuality_accepted holds, otherwise the opposite; if attracted to neither, the opposite sex. Runs on a character.

label: Women or men
summary: Gives "women" or "men", whichever the character is attracted to.
details: Same rules as AttractionWomanMan: one sex if attracted to only that sex; if attracted to both, the same sex as the character when the rite check homosexuality_accepted holds, otherwise the opposite; if attracted to neither, the opposite sex. Runs on a character.

label: Augousta or Augoustus
summary: Gives the title "Augousta" for a woman or "Augoustus" for a man.
details: Augousta when the character is female, Augoustus otherwise. Runs on a character.

label: Board game counter skill (diplomacy)
summary: Gives the name of the skill paired against diplomacy in a board game: martial, stewardship, intrigue, learning or prowess.
details: A board game round has three skills saved as bg_skill_a, bg_skill_b and bg_skill_c. When diplomacy is skill a, it gives the name of skill c; when diplomacy is skill b, skill a; when it is skill c, skill b. That is why the list holds the five other skills, three times over. The first four are written as game-concept links. Runs on a character. Similar texts exist for each other skill.

label: Board game counter skill (intrigue)
summary: Gives the name of the skill paired against intrigue in a board game: diplomacy, martial, stewardship, learning or prowess.
details: A board game round has three skills saved as bg_skill_a, bg_skill_b and bg_skill_c. When intrigue is skill a, it gives the name of skill c; when intrigue is skill b, skill a; when it is skill c, skill b. The list therefore holds the five other skills, three times over. Runs on a character.

label: Board game counter skill (learning)
summary: Gives the name of the skill paired against learning in a board game: diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue or prowess.
details: A board game round has three skills saved as bg_skill_a, bg_skill_b and bg_skill_c. When learning is skill a, it gives the name of skill c; when learning is skill b, skill a; when it is skill c, skill b. The list therefore holds the five other skills, three times over. Runs on a character.

label: Board game counter skill (prowess)
summary: Gives the name of the skill paired against prowess in a board game: diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue or learning.
details: A board game round has three skills saved as bg_skill_a, bg_skill_b and bg_skill_c. When prowess is skill a, it gives the name of skill c; when prowess is skill b, skill a; when it is skill c, skill b. The list therefore holds the five other skills, three times over. Runs on a character.

label: Board game counter skill (stewardship)
summary: Gives the name of the skill paired against stewardship in a board game: diplomacy, martial, intrigue, learning or prowess.
details: A board game round has three skills saved as bg_skill_a, bg_skill_b and bg_skill_c. When stewardship is skill a, it gives the name of skill c; when stewardship is skill b, skill a; when it is skill c, skill b. The list therefore holds the five other skills, three times over. Runs on a character.

label: Board game counter skill (martial)
summary: Gives the name of the skill paired against martial in a board game: diplomacy, stewardship, intrigue, learning or prowess.
details: A board game round has three skills saved as bg_skill_a, bg_skill_b and bg_skill_c. When martial is skill a, it gives the name of skill c; when martial is skill b, skill a; when it is skill c, skill b. The list therefore holds the five other skills, three times over. The key is written with a lowercase "martial", unlike its siblings. Runs on a character.

label: Board game decider
summary: Gives the object that decides moves in a board game: a cowrie, a die or a quill.
details: It depends on the game (saved as scope:bg_system): pachisi uses cowrie shells; hnefatafl, tabula and chess use a die; go and fidchell have no randomiser, so they get the fallback, a quill. Runs on a character.

label: Board game piece
summary: Gives the word for a game piece in the current board game: token, piece, counter or stone.
details: It depends on the game (saved as scope:bg_system): token for pachisi, counter for tabula, stone for go, and piece for hnefatafl, fidchell and chess (chess is the fallback). Runs on a character. The plural form is BG_GamePiecePlural.

label: Board game pieces
summary: Gives the plural word for the game pieces of the current board game: tokens, pieces, counters or stones.
details: It depends on the game (saved as scope:bg_system): tokens for pachisi, counters for tabula, stones for go, and pieces for hnefatafl, fidchell and chess (chess is the fallback). Runs on a character. The singular form is BG_GamePiece.

label: Board game name
summary: Gives the name of the current board game: pachisi, hnefatafl, tabula, go, fidchell or chess.
details: It reads the game saved as scope:bg_system; chess is the fallback. Lowercase. A version with a game-concept link is BG_GameType_Concept. Runs on a character.

label: Board game name (link)
summary: Gives the name of a board game as a game-concept link: pachisi, hnefatafl, tabula, go, fidchell or chess.
details: Unlike BG_GameType, it picks by where the character's capital province lies (each game has a region), with chess as the fallback. Each name is a link to that game's concept. Runs on a character.

label: Board game name (dark link)
summary: Gives the name of a board game as a game-concept link in the dark style: pachisi, hnefatafl, tabula, go, fidchell or chess.
details: Same games and region checks as BG_GameType_Concept (the character's capital province), but the links use a different display style (the name says "dark"; the input does not say why). Runs on a character.

label: Regional board game name
summary: Gives the name of a board game: pachisi, hnefatafl, tabula, go, fidchell or chess.
details: Picks by region like BG_GameType_Concept (the character's capital province if they are a ruler, otherwise their location), with chess as the fallback. Random picking is on, so if several games fit the game picks one at random. Runs on a character.

label: Random compass direction
summary: Gives a compass direction with its article: a Northern, a Western, an Eastern or a Southern.
details: Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character.

label: Board game expression
summary: Gives a facial expression of a player: scornful smirk, confident grin, competitive grimace, questioning frown, or quailing.
details: The game compares the players' cumulative skill scores (a comparison value): scornful when the opponent is arrogant or the value is -20 or lower; confident above -20 up to -10; competitive grimace above -10 up to 10; questioning frown above 10 up to 20; quailing above 20. Runs on a character.

label: Board game move type
summary: Gives the name of a move: Gambit, Cross, Stratagem, Feint or Rush.
details: Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character.

label: Random rank (possessive)
summary: Gives a noble rank in the possessive form, such as Baron's or Baroness', Count's or Countess', for a duke, king or emperor too.
details: Ten entries: five ranks (baron, count, duke, king, emperor), each in a female and a male form; the character's sex decides which form fits. Random picking is on, so the game picks a rank at random. Runs on a character.

label: Barony town type
summary: Gives the kind of settlement a barony is: city, castle town, town or village.
details: Checked in order: city when the county's development is above medium; castle town when the barony's province has a fort level above 0; town when development is between the bad and medium levels; village when below bad. Runs on a title.

label: Historical battle description
summary: Gives the description of a famous historical battle at a point of interest, with victor, defeated, date and a short story.
details: There are 24 battles (Tours, Lechfeld, Hastings, Stamford Bridge, Manzikert and others). Each text names the people through their history IDs. Runs on a province.

label: Battle description intro
summary: Gives the opening sentence of a generated battle description: the two sides meeting, an attack, a defence, or fallback versions.
details: The texts use placeholders for the province, the commander, the enemy commander and their culture. The attacker and defender fallback entries appear twice. Runs on a province.

label: Battle description middle
summary: Gives the turning-point sentence of a generated battle description, such as a berserker, varangians, archers or heavy infantry breaking through.
details: Entries are picked from variables saved on the province: a berserker or varangian brave knight first, then a brave knight with archers, heavy infantry, light cavalry, heavy cavalry or pikemen, then the same units without a knight. Texts use placeholders for the brave knight, the commander and the enemy's culture. Runs on a province.

label: Battle description outcome
summary: Gives the sentence about how the fighting ended, such as enemy morale shattered, foes destroyed, chaos or a loss.
details: Eight entries, each in a version that continues the sentence and a "Fled" version that ends it. Runs on a province.

label: Battle description ending
summary: Gives the last sentence of a generated battle description: the enemy commander was captured, slain, fled in chaos or retreated in order.
details: The texts name the enemy commander. Runs on a province.

label: Historical battle name
summary: Gives the name of a famous historical battle, such as "The Battle of Tours" or "The Battle of Hastings".
details: There are 24 battles; it pairs with BattlePoIDescriptionHistorical. Runs on a province.

label: Become tributary name
summary: Gives the name of the "become tributary" interaction: "Acknowledge Hegemon" or, otherwise, "Submit to Suzerain".
details: The hegemony text is used when the character's primary title is of the hegemony tier; otherwise the fallback is used. Runs on a character.

label: Sacred tree
summary: Gives the name of a sacred tree of a religion, such as the Divine Haoma Tree, the Sacred Cypress of Kashmar or the Sacred Oak of Thor.
details: Eight entries, including Alatyr, Somb, Kalpavriksha and a general one. Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character. Used for pedestal artifacts.

label: Bad brew adjective
summary: Gives a disgusted adjective for a bad drink, such as nauseating, repulsive, foul or vile.
details: There are 30 words. Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character.

label: Bad brew noun
summary: Gives a noun for a bad drink: mixture, concoction, brew, cocktail, beverage or blend.
details: Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character.

label: Good brew adjective
summary: Gives a praising adjective for a good drink, such as delightful, wonderful, exquisite or superb.
details: There are 28 words. Random picking is allowed. Runs on a character.

label: Brew type
summary: Gives the name of a drink such as Dark Ale, Strong Ale, Barley Wine, Mead or Honey Ale.
details: There are 24 entries, from regular ales to monastic ones. Blessed Brew and Sanctuary Ale need a rite that allows breweries; Benedictine Brew, Priors Ale and Friars Brew need the Catholic faith. Random picking is on. Runs on a character.

label: Childish brew word
summary: Gives a fond word such as Favorite, Preferred, Beloved, Cherished, Favored or Best-loved.
details: Going by the name (childish) it is meant for a child's drink; the input shows no condition for this. Random picking is on. Runs on a character.

label: Buddhist relic
summary: Gives the name of a Buddhist relic, such as the Tooth, Bone, Robes or Alms-bowl of the Buddha.
details: Eight entries; the last is a branch of the Bo tree. Runs on a character.

label: Buddhist relic name
summary: Gives the name of a Buddhist relic, such as the Tooth, Bone, Robes or Alms-bowl of the Buddha.
details: It is almost the same list as BuddhismRelic, but the last four entries use "_name" keys for the tongue, hair, sarira and Bo branch. Runs on a character.

label: Chariot race wager tooltip
summary: Gives a sentence saying how much gold the player wagered on whom to win or place in a chariot race.
details: The text shows the player's wager value with a gold icon, and the name of the charioteer or team picked. Runs on a character.

label: Cat eye color
summary: Gives the eye color of the character's pet cat: blue, yellow, green, amber, copper or emerald.
details: It reads the color stored on the pet cat story the character owns (the variable cat_eye_color). Runs on a character.

label: Cat eye color (any scope)
summary: Gives the eye color of a pet cat: blue, yellow, green, amber, copper or emerald.
details: Same colors as CatEyeColor, but it reads the variable cat_eye_color directly on whatever it is used on (it works on any kind of thing).
